log: Read all 14 photographs of the owner's own unit, serial 126072.
Side-button glyphs confirmed at full resolution: circled B over P on one rail, T over L on the other.
Pulled the real 1900X manual (48pp) from dogtra.com — the 1900S manual that search returns is a different generation and was discarded.
Opened BioDigital Human at desktop and iPad landscape. Found the no-login route: /explore walls you, /widget does not.
Sampled the Highland Canine mark and white-balanced it: blue #1560A6, orange #CF8B3E.
Scaffolded ~/Desktop/E-COLLAR-1900X (the old build at E-COLLAR-3D is untouched and read-only).
Confirmed the vendored Three.js is r128 UMD — no ES modules, no CDN.
Wrote the module contract so parallel builders cannot overwrite each other.
Round 1 critic: ours rendered nothing at all — lost on all four judged axes by absence.
Round 2 critic found a real defect: one failed mesh raised an error veil across ALL FOUR tabs and cached the rejection, so it could never retry. Fixed at the root — the veil is now per-pane.
Round 3 critic: every hard gate passes under its own verification. Remaining gap is framing, not correctness.
Checked the E-COLLAR-3D repo — clean and matching origin. The commit at 15:11 is your own parallel session, not an agent of mine. Nothing reverted.

Round 4 critic operated both apps rather than screenshotting them, and measured: the active label "01 Antenna" sat 100% underneath the Reset view chip; pills 03/04 overlapped by 24x26px; "01 Strap" was clipped to "01 Stra"; a 140px vertical drag rolled the collar upside down.

It also listed what ours already beats BioDigital on, so the next builder does not regress it: the labelled Reset view (theirs is an unlabelled crosshair), hotspots that say what is clickable before you click, manual citations in the reference column, and the 414px layout.
Rounds 5-9 launched: a real collision solver, clamping, a stable up axis, occlusion handling and non-crossing leader lines — built once in the shared stage, since all four tabs mount on it.
Session usage limit hit at 18:10 — nine of ten agents were killed. No work was lost; round 5 had already written to disk.

Round 5 replaced the push-apart hack with a real solver: hotspots are packed onto a fitted ring whose radii are capped so a pill is wholly inside the layer by construction — nothing is clamped, so nothing can be cropped.

Leader crossings are now prevented by monotone ordering, plus an uncrossing pass that provably terminates, plus a final check that demotes any surviving crossing to a plain dot. "No crossings" became a guarantee rather than a tendency.
TrackballControls swapped for OrbitControls with the polar angle clamped — the model can no longer be rolled onto its side or inverted.
models.js split into models-receiver.js and models-transmitter.js, so opening tab 1 no longer parses 1.4MB of transmitter nobody asked for.

Round 5 measured across 360 orientations (2 models x 3 viewports x 3-4 elevations x 24 azimuths): ZERO pill overlaps, ZERO clipped pills, ZERO toolbar collisions, ZERO leader crossings — including 12 transmitter parts inside a 414x284 layer.
Five successive 2000px vertical drags each stopped dead at 170.83 degrees. The model can no longer be tumbled into a pose you cannot recover from.
Critic found a real honesty bug: the no-WebGL copy promises drills that were never written. Fixing it is part of building them.
Corrected the build contract — your 15:11 commit removed the rigid head cut, so the old description would have sent builders backwards.
Tabs 3 and 4 launched in parallel, each with its own builder and critic, each required to complete its own drill to a verdict before reporting.
Both drills built and both complete a full run: fit reaches a 4/4 score, level runs 1-to-verdict.
Tab 3 critic caught an invented manufacturer claim. Verified against the manual myself before letting the builder act: p.43 never mentions longer posts, and prescribes trimming the coat instead.
Tab 4 critic caught a logic bug that undermines the teaching: the verdict was reading the hidden threshold rather than the run log, so it could report a response that never happened.

Fed two new manual findings back to the builders: the p.43 troubleshooting ORDER puts contact-with-skin above raising the level, and the manual does supply some of the tells (neck movement, head shaking, looking over the shoulder, "may be very subtle").
Fit round 2: a correct fit scores 4/4 and each of the four wrong fits scores 3/4 with a specific, real cost. The critic called the marking card the best thing in the app.
Removed the false claim about longer contact posts from app.js myself — it survived a round only because my module contract gave that file to a different owner. Verified gone from every file.
Rewrote the no-WebGL fit copy: it promised marking on three decisions when the drill marks four, and omitted the coat — the one the tab exists for.

HARNESS LIMIT FOUND: critics cannot operate BioDigital. The shared browser pane runs backgrounded, so its 3D scene is frozen and synthetic clicks reach no page at all. Static comparison works; operated comparison does not.

Level drill VERIFIED fixed: six runs, log beside verdict, three deliberate misses at threshold. It now says "you sent level 11 three times and she answered twice" and reveals the threshold separately rather than claiming she answered when she did not.
Fit verifier disproved the original bug report — nothing ever stops being drawn — then found the real fault: the pass band is on the dog's head, not its neck.
The guard added last round was half dead code: its off-the-neck arm can never fire, because the threshold was picked to keep the old default inside the band rather than measured against the neck.
This also contaminates tab 4, which stands the dog in that same default fit — so the working-level dog is wearing the collar round its face too.
New round mandates measurement over eyeballing: find the jaw line and the shoulder on dog.glb by raycasting, derive the band from that, and prove it with lateral screenshots at every band boundary.
Fit band re-derived by measurement, not by eye: sliders 42-56, default 49. The old default 72 — a strap across the cheek — is now correctly marked 3/4.
That fix exposed the last contradiction: tab 4 was standing the dog in height 0.80, which tab 3 now fails as "round the jaw". The two drills were teaching opposite things about the same collar.
Fixed it structurally rather than by copying the number across — tab 4 now reads tab 3's published answer at load, so they cannot drift apart again whichever tab the student opens first.

Also fixed a copy bug the verifier caught in the opposite direction: the app said "the strap is round the jaw" for five steps where the strap was demonstrably still on the neck. It now degrades honestly.
Final whole-app verification running: both drills at both widths, all gates in one session, teaching accuracy against the manual, and a blind static comparison.

Final pass caught the longer-posts falsehood STILL LIVE in parts.js — tab 1 contradicted tab 3 on the same part, under a manual citation. My earlier check grepped three files and missed the data file.
Fixed it, and verified in the browser this time rather than by grep: tab 1 now carries the p.43 clip-the-hair remedy and states no longer pair is in the box.
Moved the "round the jaw" boundary from 62 to 66 — the verifier proved 61 and 62 are photographically the same picture, so the old boundary called a strap on the neck a strap on the jaw.
Verified live: 42-51 "clear of the shoulder", 52-56 "behind the ears", 57-65 "riding up onto the head", 66+ "round the jaw". Console: no logs at all.
Rewrote a stale comment that told the next developer level.js carries its own copy of the fit numbers — following it would have re-created the bug that made the two drills contradict each other.
